clue.text: Old William's title of respect for a portly woman?

parts.note: portly means stout or fat
a woman is referred to as her

explanation.surface: Someone wonders how an elderly man named William might politely address a stout lady.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewis Carroll's poem opens 'You are old, Father William', so Old William's honorific is the priestly or paternal form of address; the question mark flags the split into a portly woman.
explanation.definitionFit: In Carroll's verse the old man William is addressed with this word as a mark of respect for age.

clue.text: Affair of one of Othello's people, say

indicators.note: say signals that the words are to be pronounced, and spelt differently

parts.note: Othello was a Moor, so one of his people is a Moor

explanation.surface: A romance involving someone from Shakespeare's Venetian general's household.
explanation.definitionFit: A love affair, especially a secret one, is a romance.

clue.text: Half-honest opening almost implying respect

indicators.note: Half means only the first three letters of the six in honest are used
almost means the last letter of the word for opening is dropped

parts.note: an orifice is a hole or opening

explanation.surface: A partly truthful introduction that comes close to showing deference.
explanation.definitionFit: A title such as Sir or Reverend is a form of address that conveys esteem.

clue.text: Wave to the canary

explanation.surface: Someone greets a pet songbird.
explanation.walkthrough: A roller is a long heavy sea wave and also a breed of canary noted for its rolling song.
explanation.definitionFit: A long swelling breaker at sea, and a breed of songbird kept for its trilling call.

clue.text: Dashing fellows eager to finish game with this

parts.note: bucks are dashing young men of fashion
hot means keen or eager

explanation.surface: Fashionable young men are keen to wrap up their sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' here is quarry such as birds or deer, which a shooter finishes off with lead pellets fired from a shotgun.
explanation.definitionFit: Shotgun pellets are what a hunter uses to bring down birds and other quarry.

clue.text: Policeman collects weapon on way to smuggler

parts.note: a bow is a weapon that shoots arrows
a street is a way or road
a runner is one who smuggles goods, as in gun-runner

explanation.surface: An officer confiscates a gun from a contraband dealer on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bow Street Runners were London's first professional police force, set up in the eighteenth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of an early London detective force were officers of the law.

clue.text: Bear loses right to represent 25 as a supporter

indicators.note: loses means one letter is taken out of the word for bear

parts.note: to carry is to bear

indicators.note: represent, read as re-present, means the letters are presented again in a new order

parts.note: 25 is the answer to 25 across, a mine passage

explanation.surface: A bear drops its right side to act as someone's backer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses right' turns CARRY into CARY; 'represent' rearranges ADIT, the answer to 25, as ATID.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved female figure used as a column in Greek architecture holds up the roof.

clue.text: Bad excuse for a round of applause

explanation.surface: A feeble justification gets a burst of clapping.
explanation.walkthrough: Salvo once meant an evasive excuse or reservation; it now usually means a burst of fire or of cheers.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a weak evasion or saving clause, and a burst of cheering like gunfire.

clue.text: Unfashionable drinks, we hear, for the laity

indicators.note: we hear shows the phrase is spoken and then spelt as a different word

parts.note: out means unfashionable, and ciders are drinks

explanation.surface: Passé beverages are served to ordinary churchgoers.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay people are not within the clergy, so they are those on the outside.

clue.text: Plant run in secluded place

indicators.note: in tells us the word for run sits inside the word for the secluded place

parts.note: a corner is a quiet out-of-the-way spot
to flow is to run, as water does

explanation.surface: A gardener sets something growing in a quiet nook.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue-flowered annual of the daisy family that once grew wild among cereal crops.

clue.text: Many a wife thus described was statuesque

definitions.text: a wife thus described was statuesque

explanation.surface: A remark on numerous spouses who were notably tall and shapely.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis the wife of Lot looked back at Sodom and was turned into a pillar of salt: statuesque in the most literal way.
explanation.definitionFit: A great many things are plenty of them; and the Bible's Lot had a wife who became a pillar of salt, a statue.

clue.text: Interrupt endlessly, perhaps, having lewd thoughts

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the remaining letters could be arranged some other way
endlessly means the word interrupt loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone cuts in constantly because their mind is on smutty things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the final T of 'Interrupt', and 'perhaps' rearranges the remaining INTERRUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Having an unhealthy interest in sexual matters is to be salacious in one's mind.

clue.text: A Russian river one's identified with beauty

parts.note: the Don is a major river of southern Russia
one is I, so one's (one is) gives I plus S

explanation.surface: A Russian waterway is said to be famous for its loveliness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as 'one is', giving I + S.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek youth loved by Aphrodite, whose name now stands for any strikingly handsome young man.

clue.text: Clan's head man backing one of our members

indicators.note: backing means the man stands behind, supporting the letter before him
head means the first letter of the word clan's is taken

parts.note: Alf is a man's name, short for Alfred

explanation.surface: The chief of a Scottish clan has a man supporting a fellow member of the group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members' means limbs, not people in a club: the fleshy back of the lower leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Members are limbs, and this is the muscular part at the back of the lower leg.

clue.text: Era in confusion about Roman law and Macedonian king

indicators.note: about means the jumbled era goes round the other words
in confusion means the letters of era are mixed up

parts.note: lex is Latin for law

explanation.surface: A muddled age concerning ancient legal codes and a Greek monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in confusion' scrambles the three letters of 'Era'; 'about' wraps that scramble round the Latin word for law plus 'and'. Lex is the usual crossword Latin for law.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great, the king of Macedon who conquered Persia.

clue.text: The Italian cheat always about to become a sinner

indicators.note: about means the word for always goes round the other two pieces

parts.note: ever means always
il is the Italian for 'the'
to do someone is to cheat them

explanation.surface: An Italian swindler who is perpetually on the verge of wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'about to become'; 'to become' is a link before the definition, and 'about' has the word for always go round the Italian article and the cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer, someone who commits wicked acts, is a transgressor.

clue.text: Be less dim — change into cloak

indicators.note: change into tells us the letters are turned into something new

explanation.surface: An instruction to become brighter by putting on an outer garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cloak' is a verb, meaning to disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: To disguise or hide one's real feelings is to mask them.

clue.text: Song has capacity to amuse not Kodaly's first, though

parts.note: can means is able to, has the capacity

indicators.note: not means the following letter is removed from the word for amuse

parts.note: to tickle is to amuse

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of Kodaly's is taken

explanation.surface: A tune can entertain, though it isn't the Hungarian composer's opening work.
explanation.walkthrough: Kodaly was a Hungarian composer, a musical decoy; only his initial K matters.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymn or chant taken from the Bible is a religious song.

clue.text: Bias writer against church worker

parts.note: a pen is something that writes
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: An author's prejudice against a parish employee.
explanation.definitionFit: A liking or leaning towards something is an inclination, a bias in its favour.

clue.text: Long ribbon found in the contessa's handbag

indicators.note: found in tells us the letters are sitting inside the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A countess's bag turns out to hold a lengthy strip of silk.
explanation.definitionFit: A band of fabric worn over the shoulder or round the waist is a long ribbon.

clue.text: Apt punishment a sublime example of the Mikado's

definitions.text: Apt punishment a sublime example of the Mikado's

parts.words: Apt punishment a sublime example of the Mikado's
parts.note: The Mikado sings 'My ... all sublime, I shall achieve in time, to let the punishment fit the crime' in Gilbert and Sullivan

explanation.surface: A fitting penalty is a lofty instance of what the Japanese emperor wants.
explanation.walkthrough: In Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera the Mikado sings that his aim, all sublime, is to make each punishment fit the crime.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mikado's lofty aim, his goal, is to make every punishment fit the crime.

clue.text: A poor performer has to talk at length

explanation.surface: A weak player is also apt to go on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a rabbit is a poor player at a sport such as cricket or tennis, and to rabbit (on) is to chatter endlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain calls an inept player at games by this animal's name, and the same word means to prattle on.

clue.text: Staff of 14, perhaps, marking time in the bar?

explanation.surface: An army officer's stick keeps the beat in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is ALEXANDER, read as Field Marshal Alexander, whose staff of office is this; a conductor marks time with one in each musical bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A field marshal's ceremonial staff, and the stick a conductor uses to beat time.

clue.text: Rum label designed to avert downfall

indicators.note: designed means the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A spirits bottle's sticker is laid out to prevent ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'downfall' is read literally as rain falling down; 'designed' rearranges RUMLABEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A brolly shields its holder from rain falling on them.

clue.text: At which we're unconfined, generally

explanation.surface: A remark on being free, broadly speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: To be 'at large' is to be free; 'by and large' and 'at large' both mean generally.
explanation.definitionFit: Big appears in 'at large', meaning free, and in 'by and large', meaning on the whole.

clue.text: A French saying or passage

parts.note: dit is French for said, so a dit is French for has said

explanation.surface: An expression in French, or else a corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a dit' is French for 'has said'.
explanation.definitionFit: A horizontal entrance tunnel into a mine is a passage.

clue.text: Stand for musicians in Kent

explanation.surface: A music rack is to be found in a south-east English county.
explanation.walkthrough: A canterbury is a stand with partitions for holding sheet music; the cathedral city of the same name is in Kent, a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both a piece of furniture for storing sheet music and a cathedral city in Kent.

clue.text: Loftiness of old city after danger is dispelled

indicators.note: after places the old city behind the reworked letters
is dispelled means the letters of danger are scattered and re-formed

parts.note: Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: The magnificence of an ancient city once peril has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is dispelled' rearranges DANGER into GRANDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Majesty or nobility of bearing is a lofty quality.

clue.text: Bit of bad luck about ambassador's papers

indicators.note: about tells us the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: a bit of bad luck is a setback, read cryptically as the word set written backwards
HE is His Excellency, an ambassador, so the ambassador's (he is) gives HE plus S

explanation.surface: A diplomat's documents bring a stroke of misfortune.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter reads 'bit of bad luck' as a setback, that is SET put back, an old-style cryptic synonym; 'about' wraps it round the ambassador's (His Excellency is).
explanation.definitionFit: Dissertations written for a degree are academic papers.
